Q3 2026
Shareholder Letter



investors.block.xyz


To Our Shareholders
At the beginning of this year, we established four principles to guide our work forward:

•Customers want peace of mind, not more products.
•Companies move fast or slow based on information flow.
•The best way to integrate machine intelligence is to become it.
•Intelligence depends on signal, and money is the most honest signal.

We used these principles to refocus how we work, what we work on, and where we're going. And we saw this compound into another strong set of results in the third quarter. We exceeded our guidance with 22% gross profit growth, 92% Adjusted Operating Income growth, and 109% Adjusted Diluted EPS growth, and we raised our guidance across each of these metrics for the year.

These principles also led us to refine the master plan we shared at Investor Day at the end of last year:

•Make our #company an intelligence, and enable others to do the same.
•Build the best intelligence to run your #business.
•Build the best intelligence to run your #money.
•Build open financial #infrastructure for all.
•Connect #neighborhoods globally.

Today we're delivering intelligence to our customers, connecting our ecosystems, and building open financial infrastructure to help achieve our financial results. Square Kiosk gives every restaurant the opportunity to have intuitive physical intelligence in every location, easing the ordering and line burden so they can focus more on their food and experience. Managerbot, which we just rebranded to Squaremates, now has an entirely new architecture and is available to Square sellers in the U.S., giving them access to intelligence and automation tools to help them save time and run their businesses better. We are planning to do the same with Moneybot, to predict and present the right interface to people with all the capabilities Cash App has to offer. We’re connecting our ecosystems in a way we never have before and are already seeing results: Neighborhoods was a key driver of Cash App scaling to 60 million monthly transacting actives in September, and there is much more we plan to do to connect local communities in the future. We’re using bitcoin and stablecoins as an enabler of Cash App’s expansion, and have begun externalizing our lending infrastructure through Cash App Score.1

1 A transacting active is a Cash App account that has at least one financial transaction using any product or service within Cash App during a specified period. A transacting active for a specific Cash App product has at least one financial transaction using that product during the specified period and is referred to as an active. Examples of transactions include sending or receiving a peer-to-peer payment, transferring money into or out of Cash App, making a purchase using Cash App Card, earning a dividend on a stock investment, and paying back a loan, among others. Certain of these accounts may share an alias identifier with one or more other transacting active accounts. This could represent, among other things, one customer with multiple accounts or multiple customers sharing one alias identifier (for example, families).

But what does it mean to "make our company an intelligence, and enable others to do the same"? We started down this path with goose, which helped us automate a lot of mundane engineering tasks earlier than most other companies, and which quickly evolved into a tool we could use for any role or task. It's now deeply embedded in our company's foundation, and enables us to help realize our vision to turn our company into a working intelligence, a mini AGI. We focused on separating our work into four layers: capabilities (the jobs we can do), interfaces (our distribution, from apps to hardware to payment wands), world models (the deep real-time understanding of both our customers and company), and proactive intelligence (a predictive engine to anticipate future needs, both for our customers and us).

Buzz is probably the greatest manifestation of the "Block as Intelligence" vision. It's an environment for building and collaborating that brings all of our ideas together into one surface. It's really great for solo work, and when someone is ready, even better for team work. It's designed to scale from a company of our size, to one much larger, and even to our smallest sellers (Squaremates is built on Buzz to offer our sellers best-in-class intelligence and team collaboration). It's model agnostic, entirely self-sovereign (meaning you can run it privately on your own network or system), and starts to reduce the dependency on tools like Slack, Discord, and GitHub.

We have so much confidence in Buzz and our related tools that we recently created a new ecosystem called Builderlab. Block was Builderlab’s first customer, but the problems we’re solving are not unique to us. Companies that want to transform how they work at scale need more than a model. They need simple, accessible interfaces, connections between existing tools, and secure ways to manage and evaluate the work agentic intelligence does. We built Builderlab to help transform how Block works, and our goal is to bring it to other companies to help them do the same.

In October we began piloting Buzz with prospective customers, and we expect to generate our first machine intelligence revenue in the fourth quarter. We have more to prove as we build a product offering and go-to-market strategy for an entirely new customer base, but we’re excited to extend what we’ve built for ourselves to others. We’ll approach this new ecosystem with the same principles that have guided us since the beginning: start small, give it soul, give time back, make it better. We're hosting an event in San Francisco on November 10 to properly introduce Builderlab.

Finally, we believe voice is the most natural way to interact with intelligence, so we created Dessa, which we view as the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built. Talking with it feels like talking with a person…full of emotion, nuance, pauses, and a natural cadence. Dessa truly pushes the frontier of deep learning models and is a significant contribution to the field. I encourage you to listen to the samples we've shared, and expect more from us in the future on how we plan to apply this groundbreaking work to our capabilities.

We believe we've meaningfully crossed the chasm of transforming our company from one that creates traditional financial products into one that streams intelligence as people need it. Thank you for your support along the way, and thank you for investing in our future.

Business Highlights
Make our company an intelligence and enable others to do the same
The AI tools we’ve built are giving us time back and helping accelerate product velocity. In October, we began rolling out model routing to all employees at Block, giving everyone access to a simple, efficient way to match their work to the right model capability. In recent weeks, AI has been autonomously reviewing and merging an increasing number of our production code changes related to low-risk, routine work so our teams can focus more of their time on building differentiated products for customers. Our focus on velocity is delivering more value to our customers faster: through the first three quarters of the year, we've released over 180 new Square features, already more than in 2024 and 2025 combined.

We’re focusing more development effort on externalizing these capabilities so others can move faster too. Buzz makes AI multiplayer and serves as a communication and code repository tool accessible to everyone. We've shipped more than two dozen releases to Buzz since launching our alpha release in July. We’ve rebuilt onboarding so a new user opens the app directly into a live team of AI agents already at work, with their existing developer tools detected automatically rather than wired up by hand. We’ve also released the governance and identity infrastructure, including an admin console, encrypted identity backups, and centralized community moderation that enterprises need to deploy Buzz at scale.

Build the best intelligence to run your business
Square GPV growth accelerated to 14% in the third quarter, the strongest growth rate since the first quarter of 2023, driven by our continued distribution expansion and increased product velocity.6 Self-onboarding continued to drive strong new customer acquisition while the number of new sellers joining Square through Independent Sales Organization (ISO) partners grew 90% quarter over quarter. Our field sales team and expanded enterprise motion continued to drive new customer acquisition, both in the U.S. and internationally, including Tommy’s Tavern + Tap, a fast-scaling full-service restaurant chain that chose Square to run its 16-plus locations across four states, and Public House Group, the popular London hospitality group behind The Pelican and The Bull in Charlbury.

In October, we launched Squaremates, our rebranded AI product for Square sellers that builds on the heritage of Square AI and Managerbot. Squaremates is generally available in the U.S. and brings some of Block’s most powerful AI capabilities directly to Square sellers. We’ve redesigned the experience to offer what we think is a leading AI product for businesses, grounded in the unique commerce, customer, appointment, and inventory data of each seller. Squaremates accesses cloud compute to take on more complex, multi-step work, such as staff analyses, drafting customer win-back campaigns and holiday promotions, and preparing purchase orders for food and beverage sellers. We plan to keep expanding Squaremates’ capabilities, including an Apps platform that lets sellers build bespoke apps connected to their Square data and existing staff permissions, and procurement agents that help sellers manage inventory and order from suppliers. We also plan to bring Buzz into Squaremates, providing sellers with a team communication and task management platform built with AI agents as first-party participants.

We also continue to innovate on hardware with the October launch of the new Square Kiosk, our next-generation self-ordering device built from the ground up around voice-enabled AI. Customers can now order by voice or touch, ask questions about the menu, and get personalized recommendations, the same way they would at the counter. Kiosk was built with larger sellers in mind, and early response from multi-unit operators has been strong. We’ve seen franchise operators who started out skeptical of kiosks now wanting to place Square Kiosks throughout their national footprint. We set out to build hardware that saves sellers time and money while helping them serve more customers, and we believe we've delivered on that vision.

Build the best intelligence to run your money
Cash App reached 60 million monthly transacting actives in September with Neighborhoods playing a key role in actives growth this quarter. We also launched Cash App en Español to better serve Spanish-speaking customers, and we continued to expand Families product functionality to help us reach the next generation. In the third quarter, we

6 Square GPV is defined as the total dollar amount of all card and bank payments processed by sellers using Square, net of refunds.
3

made the flow from a managed Cash App Account for Kids to a sponsored teen account smoother so customers can keep growing with Cash App as their financial needs evolve.

In the third quarter, we continued to focus our building and partnership efforts on better serving modern earners, the estimated 70% of Cash App monthly transacting actives who earn income through a combination of freelancing, content creation, and hourly or gig work. We launched our pilot of Earn in P2P, a no-fee way to accept payments and track more of your earnings easily in Cash App. In September, we launched a partnership with Workday that lets eligible employees choose Cash App for direct deposit during payroll onboarding, and in October we announced a partnership with UKG to join their Frontline Worker Network. We’re also expanding the ways platforms can pay earners directly into Cash App, and we’ve begun testing ways for customers to access their pay as they earn it, rather than waiting for payday, whether or not their employer works with us.

Cash App Tags became generally available in August, and we're seeing this new hardware deepen engagement with Cash App. Customers who ordered a Tag before September spent more in the month after their order than in the month before, with the largest increase among those who had been less active users of Cash App Card. Since general availability in August, one in five Tag orderers is a new or re-engaged Card active. We plan to continue to expand the Cash App Tags platform with new form factors and partnerships while continuing to execute on our broader commerce network strategy. In the third quarter, Fanatics chose Afterpay as its preferred buy now, pay later partner, and Afterpay Pay Monthly launched in Australia, with Apple as our flagship launch partner. Cash App Pay momentum also continued as Roblox added Cash App Pay functionality and we signed distribution partnerships with Checkout.com, Fiserv, and Finix.

Build open financial infrastructure for all
For the past six years, we've used our credit infrastructure and underwriting expertise to deliver liquidity solutions to Cash App customers. Now we're opening our capabilities up to others. In September, we announced that Cash App Score will be made available to lenders through Nova Credit, our first step in bringing Cash App's underwriting to more use cases. We expect to sign more partnerships in the future.

Connect neighborhoods globally
In August, we auto enrolled over 30,000 new seller locations onto Neighborhoods, our loyalty, discovery, and rewards experience that connects Square sellers with consumers, growing the Neighborhoods network over 10x from June. As of September, sellers on Neighborhoods represent nearly $5 billion in annualized GPV, up nearly 5x since June, and Cash App actives that have engaged with Neighborhoods grew over 5x in September compared to June. We continued to see strong per-seller engagement. Sellers that have been live on Neighborhoods for over a year averaged over 1,000 followers, with 10% of their GPV on Neighborhoods. We plan to continue expanding the Neighborhoods network further while continuing to innovate on the product to make Neighborhoods more valuable to sellers and their customers. We’re also focused on increasing the connectivity between Neighborhoods and Square products like Loyalty and Square Online as well as expanding Neighborhoods functionality across more Square hardware, building on early rollouts on Square Stand and Reader.





4

2027 Preliminary Outlook
We expect Block to perform meaningfully better in 2026 than the expectations we outlined at Investor Day in November 2025.7 In 2027, we expect momentum to continue, with Block gross profit expected to grow at least 15% year over year as our investments in AI and our broader focus on velocity drive sustained growth at scale. We expect Adjusted Operating Income to grow 30% year over year to $4.575 billion as we expand margins while still investing meaningfully to sustain long-term growth. In Square, our investments in distribution expansion are beginning to compound, and we expect to accelerate GPV growth for the third consecutive year, with gross profit growing roughly in line with GPV. In Cash App, we expect at least low-single-digit actives growth and strong growth in both Commerce Enablement and Financial Solutions gross profit.8 Neighborhoods has started to connect Square and Cash App, while our investments in AI are laying the foundation for what we believe will become Block’s next ecosystem.

Square
Gaining share in the U.S. and expanding further in international markets
We estimate more than half of Square’s addressable market in the U.S. is still using legacy incumbent solutions. In 2026, we’ve expanded product functionality and ramped investments across every distribution channel we operate in to serve even more customers in this massive market. Year to date through August, self-onboarded new volume added has grown at the best rate in over a decade.9 We’ve continued to scale field sales, and we now have over 400 ISO partners onboarded. We’ll continue to invest in compounding these growth curves in 2027.

Outside the U.S., the share of sellers on legacy solutions is even greater, and we've grown faster. We've delivered over 20% constant currency GPV growth in each quarter for the past six years, and we expect to sustain that strength in 2027. We've signed ISO partnerships in the U.K., Canada, Australia, Ireland, France, and Spain. We’re hiring field sales
across several markets, and we’re exploring partnerships that could transform the scale of our business in select countries.

Square GPV growth translating to gross profit growth
As of September, only 16% of our U.S. sellers use monetized software, and we see opportunities to innovate on
pricing and packaging to drive software attach higher next year. Squaremates is now generally available in the U.S. and in 2027 we plan to scale its automation capabilities further to add more value to more sellers. Beyond AI, we believe no one can match Neighborhoods and our ability to deliver loyalty, marketing, and discovery solutions to sellers, on their terms, while enabling them to own their customer relationships.

Cash App
We built Cash App into one of the most successful consumer fintechs in the world by doing two things well: developing unique ways to reach customers who want to try our product, and consistently delivering more value to them through product innovation. That is the entire growth algorithm, simple to say and brutally hard to execute. It is how we’ve evolved from a P2P app into a full financial services app serving tens of millions of customers, and it is how we plan to sustain growth as Borrow growth normalizes. As of September, Cash App is now over $8 billion in annualized gross profit, with 60 million monthly transacting actives, the fourth largest debit program in the U.S., and over $75 billion in annualized consumer lending origination volume.10 We are still just getting started.

We have multiple initiatives to grow Cash App actives
We are expanding the audiences we can serve with Cash App, and we believe Neighborhoods, Cash App Families,
and Cash App global expansion will be the driving forces behind long-term Cash App actives growth. We believe that almost every American shops at a Square seller in a given year, and we will soon be able to reach them across all Square hardware devices through Neighborhoods.11 For new actives who join through Neighborhoods, we're planning multiple engagement strategies, starting with introducing them to Cash App's commerce products. Beyond Neighborhoods, we see meaningful opportunities to expand our Teens and Families products through a focus on enhancing the experience for sponsors, making it easier for teens to graduate accounts, and introducing products that reinforce healthy financial habits. We continue to focus on helping modern earners by establishing deeper primary banking relationships.12 We plan to make it easier to set up direct deposit, expand the ways customers can access their pay as they earn it, and evolve Cash App Green so customers unlock more benefits as they bring more of their financial lives to Cash App. The needs of modern earners aren’t unique to people in the U.S., and in 2027 we plan to build more capabilities for a global audience.

Growing Cash App Commerce Enablement through volume growth and monetization rate expansion13
As of September, 28 million monthly transacting actives used Cash App Card, which means 32 million did not. We have more ways to drive commerce attach rates than ever before, including new Cash App Tags form factors and partnerships, growing Cash App Pay and Afterpay merchant partnerships, and expanded Afterpay Pre-Purchase and Post-Purchase eligibility. We expect to serve more customers as our commerce product set expands, and we have meaningful room to expand our relationship with customers who already use our commerce products. The median American spends $1,650 a month on credit and debit cards. Our median commerce active spends $217 a month on Cash App, and we expect to continue to expand our monetization rate as we drive engagement higher: as of September, only 10% of Cash App Card and Cash App Pay actives use a BNPL product, and we see nearly 3x higher gross profit for actives who use BNPL compared with those who don't.

Borrow growth driving Cash App Financial Solutions growth
We believe we continue to have opportunities to expand Borrow limits and eligibility while sustaining strong variable profit margins and industry-leading returns on capital. As of September, the average Borrow limit was $300, compared to the highest limits we offer of $1,500. We expect to increase average limits over the next several years as more

Investing in long-term sustainable growth
We view risk loss as an input to maximizing variable profit across our lending products.14 Since launching Square Loans in 2014, we've been able to hold loss rates consistent with our target while meaningfully expanding eligibility to more and more customers. Every annual Square loan cohort has performed in line with or better than our 4% loss target, and we’ve been able to grow Square Loans at a 27% CAGR over the past decade because of our disciplined underwriting approach, proprietary data, and world-class expertise. We are taking the same approach, with the same competitive differentiators, with Cash App Consumer Lending. Over the past two years, Cash App Consumer Lending originations growth compounded at 45%. Cash App Consumer Lending variable profit compounded at nearly the
same rate. We see meaningful ecosystem benefits beyond the returns we generate on our lending products: deeper engagement with Cash App Commerce functionality, higher primary banking attach rates, and ultimately higher gross profit per active, excluding the economics from Borrow.

In 2027, we expect to ramp investments in several long-term strategic growth initiatives beyond lending, most notably scaling Neighborhoods and AI solutions externally. Our growth guidance does not rely on these initiatives, but we believe they can become meaningful drivers of durable growth, and we will scale them with the same discipline we apply to our core growth investments. Those core growth investments have delivered strong returns in 2026: year to date through August, we’ve seen an estimated five-quarter payback for Square new volume added, with each of
self-onboarding, field sales, and ISO distribution operating in line with or better than our return and payback investment thresholds.15 In Cash App, we’ve seen less than a three-quarter payback on our performance marketing and referral investments.16 Beyond go-to-market, we’ve expanded our ability to drive velocity with AI tooling in a thoughtful way, building evaluation techniques that help us understand model specific ROI on a wide range of engineering tasks. We plan to keep investing in increasing velocity in 2027, especially since many of these investments benefit our external AI products too. We believe the most valuable investments we can make are in sustaining long-term gross profit growth, which is where we are focused in 2027 as we drive toward 30% Adjusted Operating Income growth.

Financial Discussion
We exceeded our third quarter guidance for gross profit, Adjusted Operating Income, and Adjusted Diluted EPS. Gross profit grew 22% year over year to $3.24 billion, with strong growth in both Cash App and Square. Adjusted Operating Income grew 92% year over year to $923 million, with an all time high margin of 29%, and Adjusted Diluted EPS grew 109% year over year to a record $1.13.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights
Cash App
Cash App monthly transacting actives grew to 60 million in September, as Neighborhoods brought more Square seller customers into Cash App. Cash App gross profit grew 27%, with strength across Financial Solutions and Commerce Enablement. Consumer Lending origination volume grew 40% year over year to $19.0 billion, driven by Cash App Borrow and Afterpay Post-Purchase.
Square
In the third quarter, Square GPV grew 14% year over year on a reported and constant currency basis, with U.S. GPV growth accelerating to 10.4% year over year and International GPV growth sustaining strong performance, growing 26% year over year on a reported and constant currency basis. Square gross profit grew in line with GPV growth in the third quarter.
Profitability
We outperformed our profitability guidance in the third quarter, with record Adjusted Operating Income and Adjusted Diluted EPS. We also achieved record Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter. Operating income was $428 million, up 5% year over year, while Adjusted Operating Income grew 92% year over year to $923 million. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $566 million and Adjusted EBITDA reached $1.2 billion. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.92, and Adjusted Diluted EPS grew 109% year over year to $1.13.

Cash App gross profit grew 27% year over year with strength in both Financial Solutions and Commerce Enablement. Cash App monthly transacting actives reached 60 million in September, and Neighborhoods was a key contributor to actives growth. We believe the ability to grow actives through the Square ecosystem is one of Cash App’s strongest differentiators.

Commerce Enablement gross profit growth was driven by Cash App Card and BNPL products, led by Afterpay Post-Purchase. Commerce Enablement volume grew 14% year over year to $56.9 billion, driven by Cash App Card and Afterpay BNPL. Commerce Enablement monetization rate expanded 18 basis points year over year to 1.74%, driven by higher BNPL adoption on Cash App Card through Afterpay Post-Purchase and Pre-Purchase. Financial Solutions gross profit growth was driven primarily by Cash App Borrow.

Consumer Lending origination volume grew 40% year over year to $19.0 billion, led by Cash App Borrow and Afterpay Post-Purchase. Afterpay Post-Purchase origination volume more than tripled year over year, and Afterpay
Pre-Purchase origination volume more than tripled quarter over quarter in its first full quarter of general availability. As of the end of September, we completed the migration of Cash App Borrow to a six-week loan construct. During this

Square GPV grew 14% year over year in the third quarter on a reported and constant currency basis to $76.4 billion, reflecting strong GPV growth from new sellers. GPV from food and beverage sellers was up 20% year over year, driven by strength in U.S. food and beverage GPV. GPV from retail sellers and services sellers grew 13% and 8% year over year, respectively. We continued to see the fastest year-over-year growth in our mid-market seller segment (>$500K in annualized GPV) compared to our other seller segments during the third quarter.  

Square gross profit grew 14% year over year in the third quarter in line with Square GPV growth. Growth was driven primarily by Commerce Enablement, reflecting stronger payments volume and increased software adoption, supported by the simplified pricing and packaging options we introduced last year. We also saw continued momentum in Financial Solutions, driven by Square Loans.26 We continue to expect Square gross profit to grow roughly in line with Square GPV for the remainder of the year.

In the third quarter, product development expenses decreased 11% year over year on a GAAP basis and decreased 12% on a non-GAAP basis, driven by reduced personnel-related costs associated with the organizational changes we executed in February. Sales and marketing expenses grew 15% year over year on a GAAP basis and grew 14% on a non-GAAP basis, driven by an increase in go-to-market investments. General and administrative expenses were up 56% year over year on a GAAP basis, primarily driven by increased accrued legal contingencies, and down 21% year over year on a non-GAAP basis. For more information on accrued legal contingencies, please see the Commitments and Contingencies footnote in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Transaction, loan, and consumer receivable losses increased 66% year over year on a GAAP basis, driven by growth
in loan volumes and product mix shifts. Third quarter Cash App Consumer Lending variable profit margin was in line with the third quarter of 2025 and improved modestly quarter over quarter, demonstrating strong returns and underwriting as originations continued to grow.27 Borrow risk loss rates remained healthy as we completed our migration to six-week loans in September. We expect year-over-year growth in transaction, loan, and consumer receivable losses to moderate further in the fourth quarter.

Key Operating Metrics And Non-GAAP
Financial Measures
To supplement our financial information presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (GAAP), from period to period, we consider and present certain operating and financial measures that we consider key metrics or are not prepared in accordance with GAAP, including Gross Payment Volume (GPV), Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, Adjusted Net Income (Loss), Adjusted Net Income (Loss) Per Share (Adjusted EPS), Adjusted Diluted Net Income (Loss) Per Share (Adjusted Diluted EPS), Adjusted Operating Income (Loss), Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) margin, Free Cash Flow, Non-GAAP Cash Flow, constant currency, and non-GAAP operating expenses. We believe these metrics and measures are useful to facilitate period-to-period comparisons of our business and to facilitate comparisons of our performance to that of other payments solution providers. GPV includes Square GPV and Cash App Business GPV. Square GPV is defined as the total dollar amount of all card and bank payments processed by sellers using Square, net of refunds. Cash App Business GPV comprises Cash App activity related to peer-to-peer transactions received by business accounts and peer-to-peer payments sent from a credit card. GPV does not include transactions from our BNPL products.

Adjusted Net Income (Loss), Adjusted Net Income (Loss) Per Share (Adjusted EPS), and Adjusted Diluted Net Income (Loss) Per Share (Adjusted Diluted EPS) are non-GAAP financial measures that represent our net income (loss) and net income (loss) per share, adjusted to eliminate the effect of restructuring share-based compensation expense, contingencies, restructuring, and other charges; goodwill and intangible asset impairment; amortization of intangible assets; amortization of debt discount and issuance costs; gain or loss on revaluation of equity investments; remeasurement gain or loss on revaluation of bitcoin investment; the gain or loss on the disposal of property and equipment; acquired deferred revenue and cost adjustments; the discrete benefits from the release of valuation allowances on our deferred tax assets; and the tax effect of non-GAAP net income adjustments, as applicable. Additionally, for purposes of calculating Adjusted Diluted EPS, we add back cash interest expense on convertible senior notes, as if converted at the beginning of the period, if the impact is dilutive. To calculate Adjusted Diluted EPS, we adjust the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding for the dilutive effect of all potential shares of common stock. In periods when we recorded an Adjusted Net Loss, the diluted Adjusted EPS is the same as basic Adjusted EPS because the effects of potentially dilutive items were anti-dilutive given the Adjusted Net Loss position.


17

Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are non-GAAP financial measures that represent our net income (loss), adjusted to exclude share-based compensation expense; restructuring share-based compensation expense; depreciation and amortization; contingencies, restructuring, and other charges; interest income and expense; remeasurement gain or loss on bitcoin investment; other income and expense; provision for (benefit from) income taxes; gain or loss on disposal of property and equipment; and acquired deferred revenue and cost adjustment, as applicable. Adjusted EBITDA margin is calculated as Adjusted EBITDA divided by gross profit.

Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) is a non-GAAP financial measure that represents our operating income (loss), adjusted to eliminate the effect of amortization of acquired technology assets; contingencies, restructuring, and other charges; restructuring share-based compensation expenses; goodwill and intangible asset impairment and amortization of customer and other acquired intangible assets. Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) margin is calculated as Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) divided by gross profit.

We also exclude from these measures certain acquisition-related and integration costs associated with business combinations, and various other costs that are not reflective of our core operating performance. We exclude amortization of intangible assets arising from business combinations from Adjusted Net Income (Loss), Adjusted EPS, Adjusted Diluted EPS, Adjusted Operating Income (Loss), and Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) Margin because the amount of such expenses in any specific period may not directly correlate to the underlying performance of our ongoing business operations. Acquisition-related costs include amounts paid to redeem acquirees’ unvested stock-based compensation awards; charges associated with holdback liabilities; and legal, accounting, and due diligence costs. Integration costs include advisory and other professional services or consulting fees necessary to integrate acquired businesses. Other costs that are not reflective of our core business operating expenses may include contingencies, restructuring, and other charges; impairment charges; restructuring share-based compensation expense; and certain litigation and regulatory charges. For Adjusted Net Income (Loss), Adjusted EPS, and Adjusted Diluted EPS we also add back the impact of the acquired deferred revenue and deferred cost adjustment, which was written down to fair value in purchase accounting, and adjust for the tax effect of the non-GAAP net income adjustments.

Non-GAAP Cash Flow is a non-GAAP financial measure that represents our net cash provided by operating activities adjusted for changes in settlements receivable; changes in customers payable; changes in settlements payable; the purchase of property and equipment; payments for originations of consumer receivables; proceeds from principal repayments and sales of consumer receivables; purchases and originations of loans originally classified as held for investment; proceeds from repayments of loans originally classified as held for investment; proceeds from warehouse facilities borrowings; repayments of warehouse facilities borrowings; and sales, and principal payments, and forgiveness of PPP loans. We present Non-GAAP Cash Flow because we use it to understand the cash generated by our business and make strategic decisions related to our balance sheet, and because we are focused on growing our
Non-GAAP Cash Flow generation over time. It is not intended to represent amounts available for discretionary purposes. Constant currency growth is calculated by assuming international results in a given period and the comparative prior period are translated from local currencies to the U.S. dollar at rates consistent with the monthly average rates in the comparative prior period. We discuss growth on a constant currency basis because a portion of our business operates in markets outside the U.S. and is subject to changes in foreign exchange rates. Non-GAAP operating expenses is a non-GAAP financial measure that represents operating expenses adjusted to remove the impact of restructuring share-based compensation; amortization of customer and other acquired intangible assets;


acquisition-related and integration costs; contingencies, restructuring, and other charges; and goodwill and intangible asset impairment. We have included Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, Adjusted Operating Income (Loss), Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) margin, Adjusted Net Income (Loss), Adjusted EPS, Adjusted Diluted EPS, and non-GAAP operating expenses because they are key measures used by our management to evaluate our operating performance, generate future operating plans, and make strategic decisions, including those relating to operating expenses and the allocation of internal resources.
Accordingly, we believe that Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, Adjusted Operating Income (Loss), Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) margin, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted EPS, Adjusted Diluted EPS, and non-GAAP operating expenses provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the same manner as our management and board of directors. In addition, they provide useful measures for period-to-period comparisons of our business, as they remove the effect of certain non-cash items and certain variable charges that do not vary with our operations. Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, Adjusted Net Income (Loss), Adjusted Operating Income (Loss), Adjusted Operating Income (Loss) margin, Adjusted EPS, Adjusted Diluted EPS, and non-GAAP operating expenses, as well as other measures defined in the shareholder letter, have limitations as financial measures, should be considered as supplemental in nature, and are not meant as substitutes for the related financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. We believe that the aforementioned metrics and measures provide useful information about our operating results, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects, and provide useful measures for period-to-period comparisons of our business, as they remove the effect of certain variable amounts, or they remove amounts that were not repeated across periods and therefore make comparisons more difficult. Our management uses these measures to evaluate our operating performance, generate future operating plans, and make strategic decisions, including those relating to operating expenses and the allocation of internal resources. These non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. These non-GAAP financial measures are not based on any standardized methodology prescribed by GAAP. Other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate the non-GAAP financial measures differently or not at all, which reduces their usefulness as comparative measures.
